claims.claim: Medipyxis submits electronically. Every claim leaves the system as an 837P transaction to Stedi.

checks.note: claim editor send path
biller send path

claims.claim: This page is the cross-walk: what the biller sees on the claim view, what the paper form calls it, what the 837P calls it, and which table Medipyxis reads to fill it in.

checks.note: true only if the 837P builders read the named tables (insurance_plan, claims, claim_lines, facility_billing_settings)

claims.finding: Neither live 837P builder reads a database table. Both transform the claim's saved JSON snapshot (billing_claims.structured_payload): frontend/src/services/stediService.ts:67-412 and backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediTransform.ts:112-460 (header comment lines 5-9). The 'Medipyxis source' column names tables (insurance_plan, claims, claim_lines, facility_billing_settings.pay_to_*) that the send path never reads.
claims.proposed_text: This page is the cross-walk: what the paper form calls each field, what the 837P calls it, and where on the saved claim Medipyxis reads it from.

claims.claim: Item 1a — Insured's ID | 2010BA NM109 (subscriber member ID) | insurance_plan.member_id | Blank rejects at the payer, not at Stedi.

checks.note: true only if a blank member ID is allowed through to the payer

claims.finding: A blank (or placeholder) member ID never reaches the payer or Stedi: assertRequiredClaimFields refuses it before the POST (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/claimRequiredFields.ts:582, called from _shared/submitToStedi.ts:249). This also contradicts the page's own pre-flight section. The member ID comes from the claim snapshot (carrier_information.insured_id / selected_insurance.member_id, claimRequiredFields.ts:413-420), not an insurance_plan table.
claims.proposed_text: Item 1a — Insured's ID | 2010BA NM109 (subscriber member ID) | the member ID on the patient's insurance, as saved on the claim | A blank or placeholder member ID is refused by Medipyxis before the claim reaches Stedi.

claims.claim: Item 2 — Patient name | 2010BA NM103/NM104 | patient.first_name, patient.last_name | Splits on the last space; hyphenated last names stay whole.

checks.note: true only if the split is on the LAST space

claims.finding: The name is one stored string (insured_name / patient_name) passed to splitFullName (claimRequiredFields.ts:425-427). For 'First Middle Last' order it splits on the FIRST space: firstName = first word, lastName = all remaining words (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/nameSplit.ts finalizeWesternOrder, 'lastName: core.slice(1).join(' ')'). 'Last, First' input is split on the comma. Hyphenated last names do stay whole (tokens split on whitespace only).
claims.proposed_text: Item 2 — Patient name | 2010BA NM103/NM104 | the patient name saved on the claim | 'Last, First' splits on the comma; otherwise the first word is the first name and the rest is the last name. Hyphenated last names stay whole.

claims.claim: Item 3 — Patient DOB and sex | 2010BA DMG02 (DOB), DMG03 (sex) | patient.dob, patient.gender | DOB is written YYYYMMDD on the wire.
Item 5 — Patient address | 2010BA N3/N4 | patient.address_* | Required by most payers even when the patient is the subscriber.

checks.note: falls back to the patient snapshot's address_* columns

claims.claim: Item 11 — Insured's group number | 2000B SBR03 | insurance_plan.group_number or group_id | Optional at the transaction level; some payers reject when absent.

checks.note: true only if group_id is a source
not a required field

claims.finding: Group number is read only from group_number keys (subscriber_information / carrier_information / selected_insurance) — group_id is never read (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/claimRequiredFields.ts:543-547).
claims.proposed_text: Item 11 — Insured's group number | 2000B SBR03 | the insurance group number saved on the claim | Optional at the transaction level; some payers reject when absent.

claims.claim: Item 17 — Referring provider | 2310A NM1*DN | Not sent from wound-care visits. | Present in the schema, absent from the wound-care submit path.

checks.note: true only if neither live builder emits a referring provider

claims.finding: Both live builders emit a referring provider whenever the claim carries a referring provider name or NPI (section_4_cms1500_form.providers.referring_provider): backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediTransform.ts:451-457 and frontend/src/services/stediService.ts:403-409.
claims.proposed_text: Item 17 — Referring provider | 2310A NM1*DN | the referring provider name and NPI entered on the claim | Sent only when the claim carries a referring provider name or NPI.

claims.claim: Item 21 — Diagnosis codes | 2300 HI | claims.diagnosis_codes[] | First code is qualified ABK (principal), the rest ABF. Decimals are stripped for X12: L97.421 becomes L97421.
Item 24A — Date(s) of service | 2400 DTP*472 per line | claims.date_of_service | Single-DOS today; the field exists per line so a future range would flow through untouched.

checks.note: true only if an end date (range) would flow through

claims.finding: Each line carries one serviceDate. Neither builder has a serviceDateEnd, so a date range would NOT flow through untouched; only the start date would be sent (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediTransform.ts:337-341).
claims.proposed_text: Item 24A — Date(s) of service | 2400 DTP*472 per line | the visit's date of service | One date per line; date ranges are not sent.

claims.claim: Item 24B — Place of service | 2300 CLM05-1 | Derived POS code | Wound-care visits derive to 11 (office) or 12 (home) depending on the facility.

checks.note: true only if the builder derives POS from the facility instead of sending the selected POS

claims.finding: CLM05-1 is the place of service the provider selected, stamped on the primary service line; nothing derives 11/12 from the facility and there is no default (stediTransform.ts:157-160 and 407-417; stediService.ts:113-116 and 353-363). A claim with no place of service is refused before it reaches Stedi: placeOfServiceCode is in ALWAYS_REQUIRED_CLAIM_INFORMATION_FIELDS (claimRequiredFields.ts:250). PR #3854 (merged 2026-10-27) made submit-claim refuse a missing POS as well.
claims.proposed_text: Item 24B — Place of service | 2300 CLM05-1 | the place of service selected for the visit | Never defaulted: a claim with no place of service is refused before it reaches Stedi.

claims.claim: Item 24D — Procedure and modifiers | 2400 SV101-2 (CPT/HCPCS), SV101-3..6 (modifiers) | claim_lines.code, claim_lines.modifier | One line per code.
HCPCS Q-codes come from tissue log entries; CPT codes come from the visit's procedure list.
claims.finding: Not checkable from the 837P builders: they read whatever codes are on the saved claim's service lines. The upstream claim-line builders (auto claim / claim editor) were not traced in this pass, so where each code originates is unverified.

claims.claim: Item 24E — Diagnosis pointer | 2400 SV107 (compositeDiagnosisCodePointers) | Current: ['1'] for every line

checks.note: true only if every line is hard-coded to pointer 1

claims.finding: Each line sends the diagnosis pointers the biller typed (letters A-L or numbers, with or without commas), up to four, through toDiagnosisCodePointers; '1' is only the fallback when no usable pointer was typed (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/diagnosisPointers.ts:64-71; used at stediTransform.ts:287-290 and stediService.ts:225-228).
claims.proposed_text: Item 24E — Diagnosis pointer | 2400 SV107 | the pointers typed on each line (Box 24E), up to four | When a line has no usable pointer, it points at diagnosis 1.

claims.claim: Item 24F — Charges | 2400 SV102 (lineItemChargeAmount) | facility_charge_master.charge_amount × units | A line without a positive charge cannot leave the system.

checks.note: true only if the builder multiplies the charge by units

claims.finding: The zero-charge gate is real. But neither builder multiplies by units: SV102 is the line's stored charge sent as-is (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediTransform.ts:248-250, 301). The claim editor prices lines from the charge master via priceClaimLine (frontend/src/pages/NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:1752-1790) and its own comment calls the Section 2 value 'charge (per unit)' (NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:1748).
claims.proposed_text: Item 24F — Charges | 2400 SV102 (lineItemChargeAmount) | the line's charge on the claim, priced from the facility charge master | A line without a positive charge cannot leave the system.

claims.claim: Item 24G — Units | 2400 SV104 (serviceUnitCount) | claim_lines.units
One unit per line for E/M and debridement; multi-unit for grafting is line-specific.
claims.finding: Coding guidance, not product behavior. The builder sends whatever unit count is on the line and defaults a missing/zero count to 1 (stediTransform.ts:251).

claims.claim: Item 25 — Federal Tax ID | 2010AA REF*EI | facility.tax_id (normalized) | Dashes and whitespace are stripped before the payload leaves — the wire wants nine digits and nothing else.

checks.note: true only if the send path strips non-digits from the tax ID

claims.finding: The live builders send billing_information.tax_id unchanged (stediTransform.ts:398, claimProviderBlocks.ts:163-178); nothing strips dashes at send time (the only normalizer was in the retired submit-claim). The value is the facility's tax_id (frontend/src/services/billingConfigService.ts:89-102), and the facility record only accepts exactly nine digits (facility_tax_id_format_check; message at frontend/src/services/facilityService.ts:710-711), so a dash normally cannot be stored in the first place.
claims.proposed_text: Item 25 — Federal Tax ID | 2010AA REF*EI | facility.tax_id | Sent as stored. The facility record only accepts exactly nine digits with no dashes.

proposed_checks.pattern: Tax ID must be exactly 9 digits (EIN/SSN, no dashes), or left blank.

claims.claim: Item 28 — Total charge | 2300 CLM02 (claimChargeAmount) | Sum of all line charges × units | Also gated against zero.

checks.note: true only if the total multiplies by units

claims.finding: CLM02 is the plain sum of the line charges, not charge × units (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediTransform.ts:346-348). The zero gate is real (validateClaimLineCharges.ts:176).
claims.proposed_text: Item 28 — Total charge | 2300 CLM02 (claimChargeAmount) | Sum of all line charges | Also gated against zero.

claims.claim: Item 32 — Service facility | 2310C NM1*77 + N3/N4 | facility.name, facility.address_* | Populated for every claim.

checks.note: true only if 2310C is sent unconditionally

claims.finding: Loop 2310C is conditional and does not come from facility.name. It names the claim's service-location snapshot (billing_claims.service_facility, from the visit's service location) only when the claim's POS is a residential/facility POS (13,14,16,31,32,33,54,55,56), or the patient's home for POS 12, and only when that address differs from the billing provider's; a home without ZIP+4 is omitted (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/serviceFacility.ts:6-50, 432-442; conditional spread at stediTransform.ts:418).
claims.proposed_text: Item 32 — Service facility | 2310C NM1*77 + N3/N4 | the service location recorded for the visit, or the patient's home for POS 12 | Sent only when the place of service names a facility or the home and that address differs from the billing provider's.

claims.claim: Item 33 — Billing provider | 2010AA NM1*85 + N3/N4 | facility_billing_settings.pay_to_* | The pay-to address, not the service address.

checks.note: true only if the claim path reads the pay-to columns

claims.finding: The 2010AA address is the facility's own address: the claim editor fills billingProviderAddress1/City/State/Zip from facility.address/city/state/zip (frontend/src/pages/NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:2566-2570), and the builders read section_4_cms1500_form.providers.billing_provider (stediTransform.ts:139-150). facility_billing_settings.pay_to_* is read only for patient statements (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/patient-billing-helpers.ts:301-307).
claims.proposed_text: Item 33 — Billing provider | 2010AA NM1*85 + N3/N4 | the facility's name and address on file | The location's own address, not a separate pay-to address.

claims.claim: Item 33a — Billing NPI | 2010AA NM109 | facility.npi or facility_billing_settings.billing_npi | Group NPI, not the rendering clinician's.

checks.note: true only if facility_billing_settings.billing_npi is a source

claims.finding: The billing NPI comes from the facility record's npi_code only (frontend/src/services/billingConfigService.ts:49-101 → NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:2762-2765). There is no facility_billing_settings.billing_npi fallback.
claims.proposed_text: Item 33a — Billing NPI | 2010AA NM109 | facility.npi_code | Group NPI, not the rendering clinician's.

claims.claim: Rendering provider | 2310B NM1*82 | provider.npi, provider.full_name | Emitted at the claim level, not per line — one clinician per visit is the wound-care norm.

checks.note: true only if no per-line rendering is ever emitted

claims.finding: The rendering provider is emitted at claim level (2310B), but a line whose rendering NPI differs from the claim's gets its own Loop 2420A rendering provider (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/claimProviderBlocks.ts:132-160; stediTransform.ts:314-317).
claims.proposed_text: Rendering provider | 2310B NM1*82 | the rendering provider's NPI and name | Emitted at claim level; a line with a different rendering NPI also carries its own (Loop 2420A).

claims.claim: Omitted when it equals the billing NPI (X12 RFI #1531/#1989).
The full 837P builder is backend/supabase/functions/submit-claim/index.ts.

checks.note: true only if submit-claim is a live path

claims.finding: submit-claim is retired: it returns HTTP 410 'This claim path is retired' before auth (backend/supabase/functions/submit-claim/index.ts:64, 79-87). Live 837P builders are transformToStediFormat in frontend/src/services/stediService.ts (claim editor / Billing Dashboard) and backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediTransform.ts (biller-submit-claim-onbehalf); both send through _shared/submitToStedi.ts.
claims.proposed_text: The 837P is built by transformToStediFormat — frontend/src/services/stediService.ts for claims sent from the Billing Dashboard and backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediTransform.ts for biller sends — and every send goes through backend/supabase/functions/_shared/submitToStedi.ts.

claims.claim: _shared/claimRequiredFields.ts runs the pre-flight check that catches most of the misses documented above before a payload ever reaches Stedi.
X12 restricts the field to three values: M, F, U. Medipyxis stores four: M, F, Other, and null (unknown).
The mapping (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/gender.ts — toX12Gender): M or Male → M; F or Female → F; Other → U; null / unknown → U.

checks.note: live: used by resolveSubscriber in both builders

claims.claim: Other and unknown both become U on the wire. The stored value stays as you entered it; only the outbound wire value is collapsed.

checks.note: no UI writer maps the stored value to the wire code

claims.claim: Claim-status inquiries (276/277) refuse U. When Medipyxis pulls status on a claim submitted with U, the gender field is omitted from the 276 rather than forced to a wrong value. Some payers respond AAA*Y*72; that failure is a payer limitation.

checks.note: true only if Medipyxis calls Stedi's 276 claim-status endpoint

claims.finding: Medipyxis does not send 276 claim-status inquiries at all: no edge function calls Stedi's claim-status endpoint. Claim status arrives as 277CA acknowledgments imported by backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediAckImport.ts. The only 276 mention is a caveat comment (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/gender.ts:42-43). There is no gender-omission logic to describe.
claims.proposed_text: Medipyxis does not send 276 claim-status inquiries; claim status arrives as 277CA acknowledgments from Stedi, so a claim sent with U is never re-sent with a different sex value.

claims.claim: On the CMS-1500 it is Item 24E, and it accepts up to four pointers per line.
Medipyxis today points every service line at diagnosis position 1 only (compositeDiagnosisCodePointers: { diagnosisCodePointers: ['1'] }).

checks.note: true only if pointers are hard-coded to 1

claims.finding: Same as cms-14: per-line pointers are the biller's typed letters (up to four) via toDiagnosisCodePointers (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/diagnosisPointers.ts:64-71); '1' is only the fallback.
claims.proposed_text: Medipyxis sends the pointers typed on each line (up to four); a line with no usable pointer points at diagnosis 1.

claims.claim: When a visit legitimately splits between two different wounds or two different underlying diagnoses, the current single-pointer emission may under-justify the secondary line.
claims.finding: Rests on the false single-pointer premise (cms-14/cms-32). The biller can point each line at its own diagnoses today (diagnosisPointers.ts:64-71). Payer denial behavior is not checkable from code.

claims.claim: DTP*472 is one item (24A) per line, and Medipyxis emits the visit's date of service on every line — same value, per-line placement.
YYYYMMDD on the wire. The claims table stores YYYY-MM-DD; the transform strips the dashes right before submission.
The 837P spec allows a date range (DTP*472*RD8*YYYYMMDD-YYYYMMDD). Wound-care visits are single-day encounters, so Medipyxis never emits a range.
Before a payload reaches Stedi, _shared/claimRequiredFields.ts refuses to submit a claim missing: Payer trading-partner service ID (2010BB NM109 — the payer routing key).
[The pre-flight refuses a claim missing] Billing NPI (Item 33a).

checks.pattern: 'Billing provider has no NPI. Box 33a is required

claims.reason: Refused at the same chokepoint, but by validateClaimProviderBlocks.ts, not claimRequiredFields.ts.

claims.claim: [The pre-flight refuses a claim missing] Subscriber member ID (Item 1a).
[The pre-flight refuses a claim missing] Subscriber DOB (Item 3).

checks.note: true only if some gate names a missing DOB

claims.finding: No pre-flight gate checks the subscriber date of birth. assertRequiredClaimFields checks subscriber.memberId, subscriber.lastName and tradingPartnerServiceId plus the claimInformation list (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/claimRequiredFields.ts:581-597); a missing DOB goes to Stedi as an empty/omitted value.
claims.proposed_text: [The pre-flight refuses a claim missing] Subscriber last name (Item 2). A missing date of birth is not caught before Stedi.

claims.claim: [The pre-flight refuses a claim missing] Principal diagnosis (Item 21, first position) and at least one service line.
On every service line: a procedure code (Item 24D), a positive charge amount (Item 24F — see the zero-dollar guard), and a units count > 0 (Item 24G).

checks.note: true only if a gate refuses a missing/zero unit count

claims.finding: Only the positive-charge rule is a refusal. A line with no procedure code is silently dropped by the builder, not refused (stediTransform.ts:235-237), and a missing or zero unit count is replaced with 1 (stediTransform.ts:251: sl.units || sl.service_unit_count || '1'), so no units gate exists.
claims.proposed_text: On every service line: a positive charge amount (Item 24F — see the zero-dollar guard). Lines without a procedure code are left off the claim, and a missing unit count is sent as 1.

claims.claim: Anything else — modifiers, group number, referring provider — is optional at the transaction level even when a payer needs it, so those rejects come back from the payer, not from the pre-flight.
Element on the subscriber loop (NM1**IL*..., DMG*..., N3/N4) → check the patient's Insurance tab, then the patient's demographics.
claims.finding: Navigation advice, not checkable by grep. Note: the patient chart Insurance tab is read-only and links to 'Manage in Billing' (frontend/src/components/PatientInsuranceTab.tsx:29-42, 170); insurance edits happen on BillingAuthPage.

claims.claim: Element on the billing loop (NM1*85*..., REF*EI*...) → check the facility's Billing Settings.
claims.finding: Navigation advice. Billing NPI and tax ID come from the facility record (frontend/src/services/billingConfigService.ts:49-101); a screen named 'Billing Settings' was not verified.

claims.claim: Element on the claim (CLM*..., HI*...) → check the coding review drawer for that claim.

Element on a service line (SV1*...) → open the claim, expand the line, check its code, modifier, and charge. If the payer names an element that isn't in the table above, send the raw payer message to Damon.
claims.finding: Workflow advice; not checkable from code.
